text:
deepti: heads-up — canary pool in eu-west3 (H100 mixed-arch) started seeing collective stalls after we bumped to NCCL 3.8.1. reproduces on small end-to-end inference runs. logs attached below.

infra-bot: canary-deploy: halted for pool eu-west3 (reason: runtime health check failures) :warning:

kai: what's the driver/cuda/kernel on those nodes? any dmesg / nvlink msgs?

ben: quick paste from one affected node (truncated):
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] nvidia: GPU efi=0 d3cold=0
[ 1235.001200] nvlink_priv: timeout waiting for link state change
[ 1236.345678] kernel: p2p: peer pcie_transfer timed out
```

maya: ran nccl-tests allreduce microbench on canary nodes before/after. tail p99 jumped from 12ms -> 85ms for 4xA100->H100 combos. throughput for batched requests dipped ~30%.

devin: likely interaction between NCCL 3.8.1 peer-to-peer algorithm and mixed-arch p2p paths + recent kernel 6.5.x NVLINK semantics. seen something similar in staging with cuda12.2 + driver 535.112.

sre-elly: can we hotpatch routing to avoid mixed-arch placements until we confirm? i.e. soft-fallback to single-arch packing or route heavy collective workloads to nodes pinned to NCCL 3.7.x.

deepti: yes — we should stop the canary rollout. action items:
- pause rollout (done, infra-bot)
- collect full nv-hostengine logs and nccl-trace for 5 affected runs
- add a temporary routing policy to avoid mixed-arch bins
- plan a controlled canary with p2p disabled

kai: routing patch idea (k8s scheduler ext):
```
# prototype: evict pods with label workload=collective from mixed-arch nodes
kubectl label nodes --selector='gpu.arch in (h100,a100)' mixed-arch=true
kubectl patch schedulerconfig ... # add soft-affinity to avoid mixed-arch
```

ben: short-term mitigation that worked in staging: set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 in runtime env for models with lots of allreduce. CPU overhead is small but prevents the stall pattern.

maya: note tradeoff — disabling P2P raised avg token latency ~8% but removed p99 spikes. worth it for now while we triage.

devin: longer-term we should add a compatibility matrix to the infra docs (driver/cuda/nccl/kernel) and have an automated preflight that runs nvlink + nccl-tests before fleet promotions.

sre-elly: +1. also we need a soft-safety-net: when collective latency degrades > 2x for canary, auto-revert and route traffic to fallback model variants.

deepti: can someone own the revert plan and the compat-matrix doc? i can take the matrix doc.

ben: i'll own the routing patch + small canary (run with NCCL_P2P_DISABLE env) and run nvlink stress overnight.

kai: i'll collect kernel/drivers from all affected pools and produce a short diff vs healthy pools.

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-4123 "nccl 3.8.1 canary stalls — investigate/mitigate" assigned to ben, severity P1.

devin: quick checklist for next steps:
- create canary subset that uses older NCCL (3.7.x) and compare
- run targeted nccl-tests (allgather/alltoall/allreduce) across mixed combos
- evaluate throughput vs cost if we need to isolate workloads to mono-arch racks

maya: cost note — isolating by arch will reduce packing efficiency, expect ~12% higher GPU-hours for same QPS until we get a proper fix.

deepti: agreed. let's meet in 30 to sync on tasks. for now rollout remains paused. :thumbsup:

sre-elly: meeting invite sent for 16:00 UTC. attach logs to INF-4123.

kai: attaching node list and quick diagnostics (in thread comment).
